\paragraph{Cheetah Run ``impossible dose'' dilemma.}
We observe a qualitatively different dose-response structure on Cheetah compared to Walker. On Walker, a narrow effective window exists around $\sigma{=}0.2$ where the CIVO prevention threshold falls below the noise tolerance threshold. On Cheetah, this window does not exist: $\sigma \leq 0.5$ fails to prevent CIVO (NVE $= 1.9\times$ at $\sigma{=}0.2$; $10.67\times$ at $\sigma{=}0.5$), while $\sigma{=}1.0$ eliminates CIVO entirely (NVE ${<}\,0.25\times$ throughout training, value $\approx$ target with no overestimation) but destroys policy learning (eval 27\%, comparable to untreated collapse). The collapse mechanism at $\sigma{=}1.0$ is \emph{not} CIVO---the critic is well-calibrated---but rather noise-induced representational damage that prevents the RSSM from learning useful dynamics. This ``impossible dose'' dilemma---where the effective dose exceeds the tolerable dose---scales with environment complexity: Cheetah's baseline CIVO severity ($8$--$108\times$ NVE) requires correspondingly stronger noise to suppress, but the RSSM's noise tolerance does not scale accordingly. The implication is that TCN cannot be a general-purpose CIVO mitigation: environments with higher CIVO severity will systematically lack a viable dose window.
